liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (3 reviews): Reviewer finds the China Cat into Rider sequence extremely hot; China Cat into Rider is called extremely hot, with the rest of set two also energetic [21][24][25]
- **Comes A Time** (1 review): Reviewer calls this Comes A Time beautiful [20]
- **Don't Need Love** (1 review): Reviewer especially enjoys this version of Don't Need Love [26]
- **Gimme Some Lovin'** (1 review): Opener gives everyone vocal turns, including a Brent and Phil vocal pairing, leading into Greatest Story [28]
- **Dupree's Diamond Blues** (1 review): Jerry delivers a good, very peppy Dupree's, typical of 1985 versions in the reviewer's view [28]
- **Stagger Lee** (1 review): Jerry has vocal trouble during Stagger Lee, which slows the song down somewhat [28]
- **Midnight Hour** (1 review): Bobby's spoken rap at the end of Midnight Hour departs from the usual routine [29]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Reviewer especially loves the first-set Looks Like Rain [29]
- Bobby and Brent weave lyrics of Throwing Stones and Goin' Down the Road together before the segue [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd85-10-26 s1t01 Crowd Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [31]
- **gd85-10-26 s1t02 Gimme Some Lovin**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [31]
- **gd85-10-26 s1t03 Greatest Story**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [31]
- **gd85-10-26 s1t04 Dupree's**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [31]
- **gd85-10-26 s1t05 CC Rider**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [31]
- **gd85-10-26 s1t06 Stagger Lee**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [31]
- **gd85-10-26 s1t07 Me And My Uncle**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [31]
- **gd85-10-26 s1t08 Big River**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [31]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-10-26.176851.Senn.MD441.strizak.flac2448** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 137 min [1]. Said about its sound: Set one has a tape flip at the end of Big River, with Big Railroad Blues fading in; Set two has a short cut after I Know You Rider, and the start of Women Smarter is missing [1]
- **gd1985-10-26.152787.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 22 songs; 139 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: A very loud buzz or hum in the first set was removed [2]
- **gd1985-10-26.sbd.miller.33929.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 137 min; rated 3.8/5 by 5 [3]. Said about its sound: A loud hum in the first set was removed by Jay Ashley [3]
- **gd85-10-26.mance.minches.18986.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 139 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer considers this a good-sounding audience recording [25]
- **gd85-10-26.sbd-set2.digib.17275.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 12 songs; 74 min; rated 3.88/5 by 8 [17]. Said about its sound: Reviewer hears tape hiss and some minor speed problems on this soundboard; Sound is decent but not pristine, with some tape hiss [19][23]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says several other 1985 recordings sound much better, and plans to try the audience tapes [19]
- Reviewer knows of no other show with that lyric-interlacing transition between Throwing Stones and Goin' Down the Road [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-10-26.176851.Senn.MD441.strizak.flac2448**: taped by Tom Strizak; transferred by Tom Strizak; source: Tom Strizak Master cassette’s (2) Sennheiser MD441 (Highs-lift On / (M) Music setting with No low roll-off filter) mounted in standard stereo configuration… [1]
- **gd1985-10-26.152787.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.flac2496**: taped by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  July 5, 2021; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell MX90/Dolby B) [2]. Also: Sourced from cassettes provided by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton, with patches from other sources [2]
- **gd1985-10-26.sbd.miller.33929.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Paul Scotton and Joani Walker; transferred by Charlie Miller, Jay Ashley; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5/Maxell MX90) [3]. Also: Chain runs from AKG CE-1 mics to master cassette, then DAT, Cool Edit 2000, and CD [3]
- **gd85-10-26.mance.minches.18986.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Cassette Masters recorded on Uher CR-240/AKG CE-1 Microphones [5]. Also: Mark Cohen transferred the analog tapes to DAT; David Minches encoded them using Cool Edit 2000 [5]
- **gd85-10-26.sbd-set2.digib.17275.sbeok.shnf**: source: S:MC>D>CDR [17]. Also: Reviewer doubts it came from a master-to-DAT transfer, guessing at least one and likely two cassette generations; Reviewer once owned a much crisper soundboard of this show and wants it circulated; Reviewer says a newer soundboard seed exists, taken straight from the master cassettes and including first set [19][21][24]

A very loud buzz or hum in the first set was removed
Sourced from cassettes provided by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton, with patches from other sources
Chain runs from AKG CE-1 mics to master cassette, then DAT, Cool Edit 2000, and CD
A loud hum in the first set was removed by Jay Ashley
